papers.title: Spinning particle dynamics around a non-singular Schwarzschild black hole in conformal gravity
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.24944v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spinning test particles provide a precision probe of strong-field gravity, yet their dynamics around singularity-free black holes in conformal gravity remain poorly constrained. We investigate equatorial motion around the non-singular Schwarzschild black hole of conformal gravity, in which the conformal scale \(L\) removes the curvature divergence at the origin while preserving the event horizon at \(r=2M\) and recovering the Schwarzschild geometry as \(L\to 0\). Using the Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon equations with the Tulczyjew spin supplementary condition, we derive the conserved energy and angular momentum in the conformally rescaled spherical spacetime and construct the radial effective potential for spinning particles. This allows us to determine the physical timelike spin bound, the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO), the degeneracy between \(L\) and the Kerr rotation parameter, and representative bound trajectories. We show that \(L\) strengthens the effective-potential barrier, decreases the ISCO radius, angular momentum and energy, and lowers the maximum admissible spin before the trajectory becomes spacelike. The orbital integrations reveal a clear division of roles: \(L\) governs the compactness of the bound orbit, whereas the particle spin governs the accumulated relativistic precession. These results establish spinning-particle dynamics as a sensitive diagnostic of conformally regular black-hole spacetimes and provide a possible route to distinguish the conformal Schwarzschild geometry from standard Schwarzschild background.
papers.authors: Shavkat Karshiboev, Bobur Turimov, Sulton Usanov, Ahmadjon Abdujabbarov, Chengxun Yuan, Hasanova Sumanbar, Gulhayo Hayitova

papers.title: 2-dimensional Metric-Affine Geometries and Dynamical Gravity
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.24945v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study non-Riemannian metric-affine geometries in 2-dimensions. We explicitly show that if the connection of the space is not metric compatible (i.e. the non-metricity is non-vanishing) then the underlying 2-dimensional manifold is not an Einstein manifold, in contrast to the Riemannian case. Furthermore we prove that in general the curvature in such spaces is specified completely by the Ricci tensor which, however, is not symmetric now. An enlarged symmetry of the scalar curvature under vectorial connection shifts is also found. We then apply our results to the study of 2-dimensional Metric-Affine Gravity Theories and discuss some special cases.
papers.authors: Damianos Iosifidis

papers.title: Extracting Energy from a Traversable Wormhole via Magnetic Reconnection: Circular Orbits and the Plunging Region
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.24947v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using the Comisso-Asenjo magnetic reconnection mechanism, we study energy extraction from the Teo traversable rotating wormhole at different orbital locations. This wormhole has no event horizon and cannot reduce to a Kerr black hole in any parameter limit. We compute circular orbits on the equatorial plane, the prograde photon sphere, and the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO). We find that below a certain spin, no circular orbit exists inside the ergosphere. Both the efficiency and power calculated from magnetic reconnection increase monotonically with angular momentum. Compared with a Kerr black hole under the same plasma parameters, the Teo wormhole has higher energy extraction power and efficiency. This is completely different from the Simpson-Visser rotating wormhole, which can reduce to a Kerr black hole, where the large spin makes efficiency and power decrease. We also extend magnetic reconnection to the plunging region. We find that when the spin is not particularly high, the energy extraction power and efficiency in the plunging region are higher than those in the circular orbit region, while for very high spin the situation is reversed. This conclusion also differs from that obtained from a Kerr black hole, where the power and efficiency in the plunging region are always higher than those in the circular orbit region.
papers.authors: Ke Wang, Wei Xu, Xiao-Xiong Zeng

papers.title: Probing the Graviton Mass through the Stochastic Gravitational-Wave Background Last-Scattering Surface
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.24950v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A nonzero graviton mass makes gravitational waves of different momenta travel different distances during the same cosmic interval. A relic stochastic gravitational-wave background (SGWB) with a finite momentum bandwidth therefore samples a shell of finite thickness, rather than the thin source shell of massless propagation from a single epoch. We describe this effective last-scattering surface by mapping the momentum and emission-time distribution into a radial visibility window in an FLRW background. The calculation uses the geometric-optics propagation relation and includes both dispersion and finite emission duration, without a small-mass or narrow-band approximation. We then calculate how radial averaging changes the angular power for an early-produced background whose momentum channels trace a common source-fluctuation field. For a scale-invariant source spectrum, moving a thin shell leaves its angular power unchanged, so the reduction in power isolates the effect of its finite thickness. For a logarithmic momentum width of $0.5$, mass-to-momentum ratios $q=0.3,1,3$ give angular-power ratios of approximately $0.974$, $0.771$, and $0.508$ at $\ell=10$. At a representative frequency of $3\,\mathrm{nHz}$, these ratios correspond to masses of approximately $3.6\times10^{-24}$--$1.2\times10^{-23}\,\mathrm{eV}$. We establish a framework that maps the graviton mass to the SGWB angular power spectrum through its effect on propagation distances and the radial window, for a specified source distribution and frequency selection. Using this framework for graviton-mass inference requires a source and detector model; the calculation here establishes the angular response rather than an observational sensitivity.
papers.authors: Hongguang Zhang, Zhengyang Qiu, Sirui Wang, Jiayi Wei, Jing Zhang

papers.title: Degenerate wormhole as a topological oscillator
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.24952v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A spherically symmetric, matter free degenerate wormhole is considered as a gravitational system with a single collective degree of freedom, the radius of its throat. The classical dynamics is determined by applying the equivalence principle to the motion of the throat, while canonical quantization reduces the dynamics to a spectral problem with the dynamical symmetry group \(SU(1,1)\). The exact solution of this spectral problem reveals two qualitatively different regimes. For subPlanckian masses, the quantum system exhibits Bohr type states characterized by a gravitational Bohr radius \(\hbar^2/(GM^3)\). For superPlanckian masses, the quantum system exhibits a semiclassical regime represented by the Einstein Rosen wormhole with Schwarzschild gravitational radius \(2GM/c^2\). Thus, the model connects the familiar quantum bound state behavior with the semiclassical geometry of a gravitational horizon.
papers.authors: Juri Dimaschko

papers.title: Accretion disks and photon rings in Palatini Kalb-Ramond gravity
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.24953v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate thin accretion disks and photon rings around a static black hole in Palatini Kalb Ramond gravity, connecting thermal emission with the optical effects of the radial geometry. At fixed orbital mass and accretion rate, the local radiative flux scales as $1/\sigma$ and the effective temperature as $1/\sigma^{1/4}$, where $\sigma=\sqrt{1-q/2}$ and $q$ is the effective curvature coupling. The innermost stable circular orbit and the critical impact parameter share their Schwarzschild values, together with an emitted efficiency of approximately $5.72\%$. Moreover, photon trajectories admit an exact angular rescaling that determines the strong deflection coefficient and the exponential accumulation of successive disk images. We construct images of an opaque thermal disk and a transparent emitting sheet, taking into account gravitational frequency shifts, orbital motion, and radial emissivity. Positive $q$ increases the local thermal emission and accelerates the accumulation of successive images around the common critical curve. Under the universal coupling assumptions associated with the quoted Solar System bounds, the fractional corrections are of order $10^{-11}$ in flux and $10^{-12}$ in temperature.
papers.authors: A. A. Ara\'{u}jo Filho, N. Heidari, P. H. M. Barros, Carlos F. S. Pereira

papers.title: Damour--Solodukhin Wormholes: Matter Sources, Observational Constraints, and Accretion Dynamics
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.24954v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the physical realization and observational properties of Damour--Solodukhin wormholes within general relativity. We first construct an explicit matter source supporting this geometry, consisting of a phantom scalar field coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics, and examine both electric and magnetic configurations. We then study the propagation of photons and derive constraints on the wormhole deformation parameter $\lambda$ using Event Horizon Telescope observations of Sgr A*. We show that, for $\lambda^2 \leq 1/2$, the shadow radius coincides exactly with the Schwarzschild value, although the radial geometry continues to affect gravitational lensing and the structure of photon rings. Using a thin accretion disk with a Johnson SU emissivity profile, we investigate the resulting optical images and examine the effects of the wormhole throat on their structure. Finally, we analyze stationary relativistic accretion and demonstrate that, for identical boundary conditions, the energy density and particle number density are independent of $\lambda$ throughout the common exterior region, while the radial velocity retains an explicit dependence on the deformation parameter. We also derive the condition $0 < w < (1+4\lambda^2)^{-1}$ for the existence of an exterior sonic point. These results highlight the observational degeneracy between Damour--Solodukhin wormholes and Schwarzschild black holes in the small-deformation regime, while identifying the geometric and dynamical effects through which this degeneracy may be investigated.
papers.authors: G. Alencar, V. H. U. Borralho, T. M. Crispim, Marcos V. de S. Silva

papers.title: Analysis of a Core Envelope Model for PSR J1614-2230 in $f(R)= R+\alpha R^{2} +\gamma R^{3}$ gravity and Tidal Deformability
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.24955v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we investigate the tidal deformability of an anisotropic core-envelope model for the compact star PSR J1614-2230 within the framework of modified f(R) gravity. The stellar interior is divided into two regions, with the core described by a linear equation of state (EoS) and the envelope by a quadratic EoS. The Tolman VII form is adopted for the radial metric potential in both regions. The interior solutions are matched at the core-envelope interface and to the exterior Schwarzschild spacetime through the appropriate junction conditions. The tidal Love number is determined by solving the coupled perturbation equations for the scalar field. The resulting configuration is free from singularities and satisfies the energy conditions, causality requirements, adiabatic index constraint, Herrera cracking condition, and hydrostatic equilibrium condition. The predicted tidal deformability is consistent with the constraints from GW170817, supporting the physical viability of the proposed core-envelope configuration in cubic f(R) gravity.
papers.authors: Ayesha Khalid, Muhammad Bilal Riaz, S A Mardan, Mustafa Inc

papers.title: Photon sphere, shadow, and polarized images of thick accretion flows around a quantum Lee-Wick black hole
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.24956v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the optical appearance of a static, spherically symmetric black hole (BH) in sixth-derivative Lee-Wick gravity with an exponential coupling S1 and an oscillatory coupling S2. From the null-geodesic effective potential we derive the photon sphere, critical impact parameter, and shadow radius. In the weak-coupling (Block-1) regime the shadow radius rapidly approaches the Schwarzschild value 3 sqrt(3) M, while in the strong-coupling (Block-2) regime the interplay of exponential damping and oscillatory modulation yields non-monotonic and, in some regions, strongly suppressed shadows. We classify the (S1, S2) plane by the number of horizons and unstable photon spheres: horizonless configurations retain a critical curve but lack a central brightness depression, and configurations with two unstable photon spheres show a shadow bounded by the inner one plus an outer photon ring. The 1-sigma/2-sigma EHT bounds for M87* and Sgr A* exclude certain strong-coupling bands. We develop a ray-tracing code that integrates exact Lee-Wick null geodesics, computes 230 GHz thermal-synchrotron emission from a geometrically thick, optically thin RIAF-like flow, and transports linear polarization via the Walker-Penrose constants. Compared with Schwarzschild, in the strong-coupling regime the beam-convolved ring diameter deviates by up to ~14%, the photon-ring Lyapunov exponent grows from pi to about 4-9, and the beta_2 amplitude rises by up to ~50% for a radial-toroidal field, while the phase of beta_2 is nearly insensitive to (S1, S2) at low inclination, mainly tracing the field geometry. A parametrized shock-cone model, motivated by earlier Bondi-Hoyle-Lyttleton simulations, shows that shock structures modulate the flux in a viewing-azimuth-dependent way without changing the critical-curve size. These are the first shadow, thick-disk, and polarized synthetic images of the Lee-Wick BH.
papers.authors: Shokhzod Jumaniyozov, Ahmad Al-Badawi, Olimjon Toirov

papers.title: Traversable wormholes from entropy-corrected holographic dark energy with quasinormal mode stability in $f(R,T)$ gravity
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.24964v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate holographic dark energy (HDE) motivated energy density profiles as viable matter sources for the construction of traversable wormholes in the framework of $f(R,T)$ gravity. Wormhole solutions are developed using entropy-corrected HDE models based on the Bekenstein--Hawking, R\'enyi, and Moradpour formalisms. We derive the corresponding shape functions and analyze the influence of the model parameters on the flare-out conditions, obtaining the parameter bounds required for traversability. The null energy condition is examined under these constraints and is found to be violated near the wormhole throat, thereby providing the exotic matter content necessary to sustain the geometry. We further evaluate the total gravitational energy and the complexity factor, showing that the internal structure of the wormhole spacetime is highly sensitive to the underlying entropy prescription. The regularity of the solutions is tested through curvature invariants, confirming the absence of curvature singularities and the asymptotic decay of the Kretschmann scalar. In addition, the generalized Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff equation is used to study hydrostatic equilibrium, where the inward hydrostatic force is balanced by the anisotropic force and the extra force induced by the matter--geometry coupling. Finally, scalar and electromagnetic quasinormal modes are computed using the third-order WKB approximation. The negative imaginary parts of all obtained frequencies indicate damped oscillations and hence perturbative stability of the wormhole configurations. Our results show that entropy-corrected HDE models, particularly the R\'enyi and Moradpour cases, significantly affect the curvature profile, structural complexity, equilibrium behavior, and ringdown response of traversable wormholes in modified $f(R,T)$ gravity.
papers.authors: Nattar Gayathri S, Zinnat Hassan, Uday Nambeesan, Saddam Hossain

papers.title: Exact ultrastatic multi-throat wormholes: Geometry, energy conditions, and optical cavities
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.24965v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct an exactly solvable hierarchy of static, spherically symmetric, wormholes with arbitrary finite throat multiplicity. A factorized prescription for the derivative of the areal radius places every stationary sphere at a prescribed proper distance while retaining elementary integrability and asymptotic flatness. The order-$N$ geometry contains exactly $N+1$ throats and $N$ anti-throats, arranged as an alternating chain of necks and finite interior cavities. Independently of this particular hierarchy, the Einstein equations imply three universal ultrastatic results. Every nondegenerate throat violates the radial null energy condition, whereas every nondegenerate anti-throat satisfies the null, weak, dominant, and strong energy conditions, with the strong-energy sum condition saturated. The same local combination $\rho+p_\ell$ fixes the radial stability of the associated circular null orbit through $V_{\mathrm {null}}''=8\pi L^2(\rho+p_\ell)/\mathcal R^2$; throats are therefore unstable light rings and anti-throats are stable ones. Finally, every finite cell between consecutive stationary spheres, each exterior cell, and the complete two-ended radial null geodesic carry strictly negative integrated radial null energy. The resulting spacetimes are exact multi-cavity optical chains whose cavity centers are locally nonexotic even though no cell can eliminate averaged radial exoticity. The first nontrivial member interpolates continuously from the Ellis-Bronnikov wormhole through a quartically degenerate throat to a double-throat geometry and admits closed expressions for its source, null average, branchwise Morris-Thorne form, embedding criterion, and traversability scales. Its vanishing Arnowitt-Deser-Misner mass follows from the specific radial falloff of the hierarchy, rather than from ultrastaticity alone.
papers.authors: Francisco S. N. Lobo, Manuel E. Rodrigues, Gabriel I. R\'ois

papers.title: Orbital dynamics and gravitational wave of Schwarzschild-de Sitter black hole immersed in perfect fluid dark matter
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.24967v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The dynamical properties of bound particle orbits around a Schwarzschild-de Sitter black hole immersed in perfect fluid dark matter (PFDM) are investigated. An analysis of the horizon topology shows that both event and cosmological horizons emerge within specific parametric regimes. Curvature invariants, including the Ricci scalar, Ricci-squared, and Kretschmann scalar, confirm the existence of a curvature singularity at $r = 0$. By utilizing the pericenter precession data of the S2 star in Sgr A*, the PFDM parameter is constrained to $0 < \lambda < 7.726412 \times 10^{5}$ M$_{\odot}$. For a source moving along a periodic orbit, the emitted gravitational waveforms exhibit two key features: (i) the orbital period increases with the ``zoom'' number, accompanied by a modest growth in wave amplitude, and (ii) the PFDM parameter nonlinearly modulates the period, leading to a slight amplitude suppression and introducing only a negligible phase shift relative to the vacuum case. These results explicitly characterize the local imprints of PFDM on relativistic orbital dynamics and offer predictions that are testable by future high-precision astrometric and gravitational-wave observations.
papers.authors: Ruifang Wang, Fabao Gao, Ruihong Yue

papers.title: Gyromagnetic ratios of slowly rotating charged Ellis-Bronnikov wormholes
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.24968v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Charged Ellis--Bronnikov wormholes, supported by a phantom scalar field in Einstein--Maxwell theory, connect two asymptotically flat regions, so a rotating member carries a magnetic dipole moment and a gyromagnetic ratio at each mouth. We construct the slowly rotating family in closed form on all three background branches and show that, within the stationary axial dipole sector and with no applied magnetic field, the first-order solution is unique. The two gyromagnetic ratios obey an exact deficit relation set by the static geometry alone. It gives $g_\pm<2$ at both mouths, bounds the deficit by two-thirds of the squared ratio of scalar to electric charge, and, through the positivity of the reduced magnetic moment, gives each ratio the sign of the mass of its own mouth; the two ratios coincide only for reflection-symmetric throats, so their difference measures the asymmetry of the wormhole. Rotation drags the two ends relative to each other in a definite sense, with a dragging profile that decreases monotonically across the throat, and the electromagnetic field carries a strictly positive share of the angular momentum on every finite sphere. Toward the extremal edge at the positive mouth the deficit closes cubically on every trajectory studied, because the redshift factor at the throat vanishes quadratically; the coefficient depends on the path. When the charge is switched off, the frame dragging reproduces known neutral results, whereas on the massive neutral branch the gyromagnetic ratios stay away from the Kerr--Newman value.
papers.authors: Safiqul Islam, Anirudh Pradhan, Francisco Tello-Ortiz, Safyan Mukhtar

papers.title: Coupling of TQFTs to QFTs and SymTFT interfaces from bordisms
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.25012v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: M-theory local models may exhibit torsional cycles and other non-trivial topology which interpolate between quantum field theory sectors localized at singularities and the asymptotic regions of the local model. We show that such structures give rise, in standard decoupling limits, to additional topological sectors which can couple non-trivially to the localized QFT. From a symmetry topological field theory (SymTFT) perspective, the physical boundary conditions associated to such local models are modified. We give a construction of SymTFT interfaces from geometric bordisms interpolating between the local singularity and the asymptotic boundary. We apply this construction to the circle compactification of a frozen $D_5$ singularity, identifying a topological interface between the $\mathbb{Z}_4$ SymTFT of the full theory and the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ SymTFT of its local $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ gauge sector. We show that the resulting coupling between the gauge theory and an additional topological quantum field theory accounts for the apparent mismatch between electric and magnetic symmetries of the frozen theory.
papers.authors: Max H\"{u}bner, Ling Lin, Daniel Robbins, Subham Roy

papers.title: Scherk-Schwarz Compactifications: From Circles to Strings
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.25014v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This review is written with a simple question in mind: what does one need to know to enter the literature on Scherk-Schwarz compactifications? It is organized as a sequence of questions that a graduate student might naturally ask, together with the concepts, calculations, and formal tools needed to work through the literature. The discussion starts at an elementary field-theory level and gradually develops toward more advanced aspects of supergravity, orbifolds, quantum effects, and string theory. Phenomenological applications are deliberately left aside.
papers.authors: Karim Benakli

papers.title: Quiver-Invariant Triality between Brane Brick Models
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.25017v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study quiver-invariant triality between 2d (0,2) supersymmetric gauge theories described by brane brick models associated with toric Calabi-Yau 4-folds. The dual theories share the same gauge groups, field content and E-terms but have distinct J-terms. We present an explicit pair of such brane brick models and identify the sequence of triality mutations relating them. This sequence returns the quiver to its original form while transforming the J- and E-terms. We explain the relation between quiver-invariant triality and the orbifold reduction of quiver-invariant brane tilings.
papers.authors: Dongwook Ghim, Juno Kwon, Rak-Kyeong Seong

papers.title: Asymmetric Orbifolds and 4-dimensional $\mathcal N=4$ String Islands
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.25020v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formulate heterotic and type II $\mathbb T^6/\mathbb Z_n$ asymmetric orbifolds preserving all 16 right-moving supersymmetries and leading to 4-dimensional islands without massless moduli other than the dilaton. We establish the consistency of the orbifold conformal field theory, including the validity of operator interpretation. In the heterotic case we classify all islands based on the $\Gamma(22,6)$ lattice constructed via the Leech lattice. In the type II case we also provide a classification of allowed $\Gamma(6,6)$ lattices and orbifold generators. In both cases we further examine whether a particular orbifold admits an archipelago of different islands arising from inequivalent realizations of the orbifold action.
papers.authors: Gerardo Aldazabal, Eduardo C. Andr\'es, Anamar\'ia Font, Elisa I. Marieni, Kumar Narain, Ida G. Zadeh

papers.title: Conformal manifolds of $\mathcal{N}=1$ orbifold theories - Part I: Marginal deformations and the one-loop spectrum
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.25021v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider orbifolds of 4d $\mathcal{N}=4$ super-Yang--Mills theory that preserve minimal supersymmetry and study their conformal manifolds, focusing on two families of Abelian orbifolds in the planar limit. We compute their superconformal indices, construct their complete single-trace BPS spectra and identify the conformal manifolds. These are generically spanned by a subset of the gauge-couplings, whose number we derive from both gauge and string theory, and a universal Leigh--Strassler-type superpotential deformation. We then construct the complete, planar one-loop dilatation operator on these conformal manifolds, giving perturbative access to the full non-BPS spectrum away from the orbifold point. This lays the groundwork for studying special loci of the conformal manifold in a forthcoming Part II.
papers.authors: Fabio Mantegazza, Elli Pomoni, Torben Skrzypek

papers.title: Stringy Corrections from Gravity: Predictions for BFSS and ABJM
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.25022v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Despite enormous progress in string theory, the leading stringy corrections to many holographic observables remain unknown. String/M-theory dualities nonetheless allow them to be determined from gravity alone. From the winding modes of one-loop 11d supergravity on a circle, we derive the leading tree-level stringy terms in the type IIA effective action for the metric, dilaton, and Ramond--Ramond one-form, in closed form as a finite supertrace over Lorentz generators. On the thermal D0-brane geometry, this gives the first correction to the low-temperature thermodynamics of the BFSS matrix model. Its coefficient differs from published lattice Monte Carlo estimates by $\approx 20\%$. With the four-form flux included, the same method reproduces the $\zeta(3)k^{2}$ term of the ABJM free energy on the three-sphere obtained by localization.
papers.authors: Aidan Herderschee, Victor Ivo, Henry W. Lin, Yifan Wang

papers.title: Actionless Branes on Axion Wormholes
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.25026v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Can a Euclidean axion wormhole extend to infinity with every instanton still suppressed? The imaginary distance bound says it cannot: some instanton must become actionless first. Calabi-Yau compactifications appear to violate the bound: several axions share the field excursion, and the instantons charged under any one of them stay suppressed all the way. We show that the wormhole can hide from these instantons but not from their bound states: misaligned central charges make a bound state cheaper than its constituents, while the axions act on every constituent. On the type IIB wormhole supported by two axions of the Neveu-Schwarz two-form, a fivebrane carrying string charge becomes actionless at large volume within two thirds of the way to infinity, for either relative sign of the axions and however they share the excursion. In S-dual variables it is a D5-brane with magnetic flux for one sign and a D5-NS5 bound state for the other. Adding more axions does not help: the same branes become actionless on every Calabi-Yau threefold, because what counts is the degree of homogeneity of the saxion sector, not the number of axions. These bound states are what the convex-hull axion weak gravity conjecture requires.
papers.authors: A. Ramesh Chandra

papers.title: Numerical Implementation and Tests of the Quadratic Effective Action for Lorentzian Spinfoam Amplitudes
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.25031v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the pure integral representation of Lorentzian EPRL spinfoam amplitudes, the integration over non-geometric variables in the large-spin limit defines an effective action for Regge geometries. Expanding this effective action to quadratic order around a flat background recovers the classical Regge action $iS_{\mathrm{Regge}}$ at leading order, supplemented by a curvature correction quadratic in the bulk deficit angles $\varepsilon$. In this work, we numerically implement this effective-action framework and validate its analytic predictions using two Julia packages: LorentzianSimplexSolver, for the computation of real and complex critical-point data, and Effective-Spinfoam, for the evaluation of the effective action. We apply this workflow to the double-$\Delta_3$ complex, the $1$-$5$ Pachner move, its refinement, and a $24$-simplex hypercube triangulation. Two complementary numerical tests are performed: first, starting from the real critical point of a flat background, we verify that the leading term reproduces the quadratic Regge action and evaluate the $\varepsilon^2$ curvature correction across a range of the Barbero-Immirzi parameter $\gamma$. Power-law fits confirm that in the small-$\gamma$ regime, the $\varepsilon^2$ correction is of higher order in $\gamma$ than the Regge action. Second, for a sample of curved geometries with finite length perturbations $\delta\ell$, we numerically solve the full nonlinear critical equations at fixed perturbed edge lengths for complex critical points. By comparing the direct action evaluation at complex critical points with the quadratic effective action, we demonstrate that the latter accurately reproduces the nonlinear complex critical-point action up to remainders of cubic order in $\delta\ell$.
papers.authors: Dongxue Qu, Sean Tobin, Hongguang Liu, Muxin Han

papers.title: Twist and Shout: defect lines on the R\'enyi torus
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.25032v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider what the entanglement between two regions of a critical system can reveal about its symmetries, including non-invertible ones. For two intervals in a two-dimensional conformal field theory, the second R\'enyi entropy is a partition function on a torus, and a topological defect line can be wrapped around one of the intervals. For an on-site symmetry this computes the overlap of the reduced density matrix with its image under the symmetry acting on one interval, and in general it defines an observable that depends only on the cross-ratio. As the intervals approach each other, the observable vanishes at a rate set by the lightest operator on which the line can end, and its monodromy is fixed by the spins of such operators. Since these spins are constrained by the fusion category, the observable detects 't Hooft anomalies and distinguishes categories with the same fusion rules. It can be computed in closed form for a $\mathbb{Z}_2$, a $\mathbb{Z}_3$ and a Fibonacci line of the $(E_8)_1$ theory, and for the spin-flip and Kramers-Wannier lines of the Ising model, where the spin-flip result agrees with an exact computation in the critical Ising chain. Averaged over a symmetry, the observable reduces to a known Jones-index bound on the mutual information. We also show that the associated twist-field crossing equations are a form of the modular bootstrap, and discuss whether the full fusion category can be recovered from entanglement on surfaces of higher genus.
papers.authors: Naveen Balaji Umasankar

papers.title: Pure integral formula of spinfoam amplitude and curvature corrections in effective theory
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.25033v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a new analytic method for the semiclassical analysis of the Lorentzian EPRL spinfoam amplitude on a fixed triangulation. We derive a pure integral formula for the spinfoam amplitude that trades the discrete sum over internal spins for integrals over continuous variables. This reformulation is free of discrete sums and provides a well-behaved action that is well-adapted to the stationary phase approximation in the large-spin regime. Integrating out the non-geometric variables yields an effective action for the edge lengths of the Regge geometry. Applying the stationary phase approximation and expanding this effective action to second order in perturbations around a flat background, we obtain the classical Regge action at leading order, supplemented by a quadratic correction in the deficit angles $\varepsilon$. This curvature correction originates from two distinct sources: a holonomy correction resulting from the new action and the fluctuations of non-Regge areas. We show that the quadratic $\varepsilon$ correction appears at a higher order in the Barbero-Immirzi parameter $\gamma$ relative to the Regge action. Together with the large-spin expansion, this yields a two-parameter expansion for the spinfoam effective action, whose leading order is the quadratic Regge action. In the long wavelength regime, the latter approaches the action of a massless spin-2 graviton.
papers.authors: Muxin Han

papers.title: Simulation-based inference for gravitational-wave cosmology: parameter reconstruction of a first-order electroweak phase transition
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.25036v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background (SGWB) from a cosmological first- order phase transition would be unambiguous evidence for physics beyond the Standard Model, with a strong electroweak phase transition (EWPT) at LISA as a prime example. Reconstructing the underlying model from such a signal is challenging, since the map from the model parameters to the spectrum is degenerate and strong transitions occupy only small and sparse regions of parameter space. We show that simulation-based inference (SBI), a likelihood-free approach applicable to generic SGWB sources, provides a reliable parameter reconstruction despite these difficulties. We first apply SBI to the thermodynamic parameters characterizing the transition, namely its strength, inverse duration, temperature and bubble wall velocity. As a concrete application, we then consider a strong EWPT in a singlet extension of the Standard Model and reconstruct the model parameters from the resulting SGWB. We find that the SBI posteriors agree with those of a likelihood-based Markov chain Monte Carlo analysis, at negligible cost per data set once the network has been trained. Using the network posterior as the proposal for importance sampling with the exact likelihood further corrects its remaining deviations, at a sampling efficiency several orders of magnitude higher than sampling from the prior. SBI thus offers a fast and flexible framework for the cosmological science case of LISA
papers.authors: Thomas Biek\"otter, Andrii Dashko, Kateryna Radchenko

papers.title: Subsolar neutron star-black hole binaries from collapsars: Gravitational waveform models and detectability in current searches
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.25040v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Detecting subsolar objects in binary mergers would be an exceptional discovery in gravitational wave astronomy. So far, dedicated searches for subsolar coalescences reported no confident detections, setting upper bounds on their merger rate. Given that standard stellar evolution is not able to produce subsolar candidates, a confident detection would point either to new physics or to unconventional astrophysical pathways. These include collapsars, where the outer parts of neutrino-cooled accretion disks around newborn stellar-mass black holes are subject to fragmentation and give rise to subsolar neutron stars, which can later merge with the central black hole. We show that current subsolar searches may miss a significant fraction of these neutron star-black hole mergers, because their templates do not account for the small mass ratios, the tidal disruption of the neutron star, and the effects of the surrounding gas. This result motivates improving the waveform modeling used in current subsolar searches and building adequate template banks tailored to these systems.
papers.authors: Vishal Baibhav, Valerio De Luca, Loris Del Grosso, Emanuele Berti, Brian D. Metzger, Lam Hui

papers.title: Entanglement entropy from fundamental strings
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.25045v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In previous work, we derived the local entropy capacity from off-shell string theory and combined it with the gravitational replica construction and flow-cut duality to normalize the entropy flow carried by physical fundamental strings. In this paper, we apply this framework to interval entanglement in holographic CFT$_2$. We construct explicit on-shell F1 worldsheets in the AdS$_3$ vacuum and planar BTZ, derive their Kalb-Ramond source currents, and show that the normalized spatial currents saturate the corresponding RT surface. Their flux reproduces both the vacuum single interval entropy and the finite temperature CFT$_2$ result. We then vary the NS-NS flux fraction. Although the total maximal flux remains unchanged, the F1 equations continuously redistribute the strings among different parts of the complement. In planar BTZ, the resulting signed flux through the bifurcation line reproduces the extensive thermal entropy and can vanish in the pure NS-NS limit without changing the interval entropy. Thus the on-shell string dynamics additionally determines its physical routing and boundary contact structure.
papers.authors: Houwen Wu, Shuxuan Ying

papers.title: $C_T$ and $C_J$ of general scalar--fermion conformal field theories in $d=4-\epsilon$
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.25055v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compute $C_T$ and $C_J$, the coefficients of the stress-tensor and conserved-current two-point functions, to order $\epsilon^3$ at any fixed point of the general renormalizable theory of scalars and fermions in $d=4-\epsilon$. We give explicit results for the chiral Ising, XY and Heisenberg models and for fixed points with emergent supersymmetry in $d=3$. In theories without a four-dimensional counterpart, fermion loops with an odd number of Yukawa vertices contribute at order $\epsilon^3$ through traces whose continuation away from $d=3$ is ambiguous; we fix it with $\mathcal N=1$ supersymmetry, by computing the two-point functions of the supercurrent and of the fermionic partner of a flavor current to four loops. In $d=3$, Pad\'e approximants closely reproduce the exact $C_T$ of the $\mathcal N=2$ super-Ising model. We estimate the universal conductivity at the charge-density-wave, Kekul\'e and N\'eel transitions of graphene to be $\sigma/\sigma_{\rm free}\approx0.91$, $0.79$--$0.83$ and $0.64$--$0.74$, and show that the exact conductivity at the supersymmetric transition on the surface of a topological insulator is $\sigma/\sigma_{\rm free}=\frac{9}{10}\,C_T/C_{T,\rm free}\approx0.654$, $10\%$ below the value previously reported.
papers.authors: Shiroman Prakash, Shubham Kumar Sinha

papers.title: Nonzero cubic Love numbers of Schwarzschild black holes
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.25059v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Static Love numbers of Schwarzschild black holes vanish at linear and quadratic order in General Relativity, while generic nonlinear tides remain less understood. We solve a specific non-axisymmetric octupolar tide at cubic order and, building on the symmetry of static General Relativity exploited by Parra-Martinez and Podo, match the result to a worldline effective field theory (EFT) using dimensional regularization. Surprisingly, we find a Love number that neither vanishes nor runs.
papers.authors: Bruno Bucciotti

papers.title: Soft Factorisation of WQFT and the Spinning 4PM Magnusian
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.25090v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive the soft divergences of $\hat{N}=-i\log\hat{S}$ in the Worldline Quantum Field Theory (WQFT) formalism, focusing on poles due to single massive-massive (Coulomb) and massive-massless (tail) graviton exchanges. Our derivation is inspired by the Faddeev-Kulish procedure, switching the interaction picture to one with an infrared-finite $\hat{N}$-matrix. Soft divergences emerging from the worldline are correlators of Wilson lines. As confirmation of this structure, we demonstrate explicitly how divergences of inclusive observables including the momentum impulse $\Delta p_i^\mu$ and spin kick $\Delta S_i^\mu$ cancel, and we reproduce the infrared divergence of the one-loop scattering waveform. Using the Magnus series representation of $\hat{N}$ and Murua coefficients, we then calculate the Magnusian $N=\langle0|\hat{N}|0\rangle$ at fourth post-Minkowskian (4PM) order, including linear-in-spin corrections. For aligned spins, $-\partial N/\partial L$ reproduces the full scattering angle through 3PM order; at 4PM order, $N$ develops a soft divergence as predicted by our soft factorisation. Using the Feynman $i0^+$ prescription, we also derive an infrared-finite 4PM Magnusian which compactly encodes existing results for the conservative momentum impulse and spin kick via nested iterations of Poisson brackets.
papers.authors: Riccardo Gonzo, Gustav Mogull, Benjamin Sauer

papers.title: Revealing galaxy assembly bias with luminosity-weighted marked correlations
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.25093v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate whether luminosity-weighted marked correlation functions can reveal secondary halo information beyond that encoded by halo mass alone, as expected in scenarios of galaxy assembly bias. We propose a controlled null test in which galaxy luminosities follow the same mean luminosity--halo mass relation and scatter, while their residuals are either (A) uncorrelated with secondary halo properties or (B) correlated with a standardized secondary halo property, $s$. Both models have identical halo occupation, galaxy positions, luminosity function, and unweighted projected two-point correlation function, $w_p(r_p)$, so their distinction is encoded entirely in the luminosity marks. At leading order, the projected marked correlation function difference, $\Delta\mathcal{M}_p(r_p)$, scales as $\rho^2\sigma_{\log L}^2\xi_{ss}(r_p)$, where $\rho$ controls the coupling between the luminosity and secondary-property residuals, $\sigma_{\log L}$ is the scatter in log luminosity at fixed halo mass, and $\xi_{ss}$ describes the spatial correlation of the secondary property. We test this framework using a DESI-BGS mock catalogue over $0.1<z<0.4$. For the injected dependence, we detect a marked-clustering deviation over $0.11<r_p/(h^{-1}\,{\rm Mpc})<1.04$, obtaining $\chi^2=30.14$ relative to the null covariance. A one-parameter test rejects the mass-only hypothesis at greater than $5\sigma$ significance ($p=2.13\times10^{-7}$) for $|\rho|>0.63$. At fixed $\sigma_{\log L}=0.23$, correlations as weak as $|\rho|\simeq0.52$ remain detectable, with the results stable under variations in the HOD prescription and modelled galaxy selection effects. These results establish luminosity-weighted marked clustering as a sensitive null test for property-based galaxy assembly bias and secondary halo information hidden from unweighted two-point clustering.
papers.authors: Joaquin Armijo, Roberta Vasallo, L. Raul Abramo, Antonio D. Montero-Dorta

papers.title: Calabi-Yau linear models with abelian bundles
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.25101v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a construction of (0,2) gauged linear sigma models whose large radius phases realize Calabi-Yau sigma models with line bundles. We study a family of such models admitting Landau-Ginzburg orbifold phases, described as asymmetric orbifolds of (2,2) Gepner models and free left-moving fermions. These orbifolds extend the Gepner construction to a broader class of (0,2) SCFTs, and reveal unexpected features, including the emergence of free fermions in twisted sectors and substantial enhancements of the left-moving current algebra. The gauged linear sigma model connects the Calabi-Yau geometry to these rational points, where the volume modulus becomes charged under the enhanced gauge symmetry and freezes at the string scale.
papers.authors: Yann Proto

papers.title: From Instantons to AdS Boundaries: Tracing the Geometric Path from Quantum Anomalies to Massive Gravity
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.25103v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This thesis studies how boundary data enter two gravitational observables: the Dirac index on gravitational instantons and conserved charges in three-dimensional New Massive Gravity. In Einstein gravity coupled to ModMax electrodynamics, we compute the index of charged Dirac fermions on Taub-NUT and Eguchi-Hanson instantons using the Atiyah-Patodi-Singer theorem, which includes the spectral asymmetry of the boundary Dirac operator. The Taub-NUT index agrees with the Maxwell result. For Eguchi-Hanson, the gauge-field contribution to the axial anomaly depends explicitly on the ModMax parameter when expressed in terms of the solution parameters. For asymptotically anti-de Sitter solutions of New Massive Gravity with Brown-Henneaux boundary conditions, a term linear in the extrinsic curvature reproduces the holographic stress tensor of the auxiliary-field formulation. At the degenerate point, relaxed boundary conditions admit an additional constrained Fefferman-Graham coefficient. A quadratic extrinsic counterterm cancels the residual power divergence. We derive the boundary Ward identity and show that the holographic and Noether-Wald charges agree for the solutions studied.
papers.authors: Leonardo Sanhueza

papers.title: Strong Coupling of Cosmological Perturbations in mLQC-I: The Hybrid Approach
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.25180v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study nonlinear perturbative consistency of scalar perturbations in modified loop quantum cosmology I (mLQC-I) within the hybrid approach. We express the quadratic and cubic Hamiltonians in a common canonical representation before imposing the background constraint and adopt a minimal sector-preserving cubic regularization. Near the pre-bounce quantum-geometrical de Sitter phase, nonlinear coefficients become strongly enhanced. The $\alpha_I^3/\kappa$ term survives the leading ultraviolet cubic kernel for fixed nondegenerate triangles in the selected frequency assignment. This enhancement occurs in four inflationary potentials, with formal suppression scales sensitive to their normalization. In an assumed factorized quartic continuation, a selected lapse contact does not cancel enhanced cubic exchange in an analytic scattering family. However, the derived quartic Legendre contribution cancels that lapse contact at $V=K_\phi$ in the Hamiltonian. The full amplitude remains unresolved: omitted quartic sectors are not proved subleading, and the formal scales do not determine a physical cutoff. For an instantaneous quadratic state initialized at the bounce, the equilateral cubic diagnostic first reaches unity at $K\simeq0.6483m_{\rm P}$. Evolution over $0\le t/t_{\rm P}\le10$ lowers this crossing to $K\simeq0.64626m_{\rm P}$. Sampled shape and independent frequency-assignment tests do not lower these thresholds. A fourth-order adiabatic ultraviolet tail can be attached without changing the tested finite modes. These results identify pre-bounce nonlinear enhancement and a candidate bounce-state window. Broader evolution and shape tests, renormalized backreaction, observational mode mapping on a consistently normalized background, and a complete fourth-order theory remain necessary to establish interacting consistency.
papers.authors: Jamal Saeed, Rui Pan, Anzhong Wang

papers.title: Multiphase Gas in High-$z$ Cosmic Sheets
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.25220v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present high-resolution cosmological simulations of individual cosmic sheets ($z=3-6$) using the moving-mesh code AREPO to study cold gas ($T\approx10^4\rm ~K$) in the diffuse cosmic web. We find cosmic sheet gas forms a fragmented morphology, evident as kiloparsec-scale variations in the neutral hydrogen column density ($N_{\rm HI}$). Fragmentation arises from the bending and disruption of the cold-dense sheet core into a multiphase medium. Nonlinear thin shell instability (NTSI) and later shear-induced vorticity drive this bending, rather than previously suggested thermal or Richtmyer-Meshkov instabilities. Higher resolution enhances fragmentation. Across a fourfold range in spatial resolution, $N_{\rm HI}$ covering fractions increase by factors of $\approx 1.5-3.5$ for partial Lyman-limit systems (pLLS) and Lyman-limit systems (LLS). An order-of-magnitude estimate suggests sheets may host a large fraction of the ultra-low metallicity (p)LLS population. Equivalent MP-Gadget simulations show qualitatively similar fragmentation, but numerical smoothing effects are present. Cosmic-sheet gas properties remain unconverged despite our high resolutions.
papers.authors: Charles Willard, Yakov Faerman, Samuel McCarty, Matthew McQuinn, Nir Mandelker, Thomas Quinn

papers.title: Holographic Duals of $SL^{(q)}(2, \mathbb{R})$ Deformed CFTs
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.25240v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the holographic bulk dual of 2D CFTs evolved by $sl^{(q)}(2,R)$-deformed Hamiltonians. Working in the Hamiltonian-adapted frame, in which the $sl^{(q)}(2,R)$-deformed effective Floquet Hamiltonian generates time translations, we construct the dual Ba\~nados geometries for the three distinct classes of dynamics: the heating phase, the non-heating phase and the phase boundary. Specifically, we show that in the heating phase, the bulk patch dual to the region between two neighbouring fixed points has a time-dependent causal horizon and asymptotes to a static AdS Rindler geometry at late times, while the non-heating phase has no horizon. We discuss how the late-time behaviour of the entanglement entropy, particularly its linear growth in the heating phase, can be understood from the bulk in two different ways: in global AdS, from the portion of the geodesic behind the horizons, and in a quotient description, from an effective shockwave produced by a boosted conical defect. Finally, for ($q=1$), we complete the holographic analysis of Ref. [1] by reproducing the exact CFT expression of the OTOC from the bulk and explaining why it exhibits an exponential growth {\it only} when the operators lie on the side of the two fixed points.
papers.authors: Somnath Porey, Baishali Roy, Rahul Roy, Bobby Ezhuthachan

papers.title: First $\Omega_{\rm m}-w$ Measurement Using Only Fast Radio Burst Observations
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.25312v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Though fast radio bursts (FRBs) are widely advocated as a dark energy probe, no valid $\Omega_m-w$ constraint has been obtained exclusively from FRB data to date. Benefiting from a rapidly growing localized sample and a novel statistical framework for modeling the dispersion measure (DM), we report the first simultaneous inference of the matter density $\Omega_m$ and dark energy equation of state parameter $w$ from FRBs alone, without external observational priors on these two parameters. We combine a multi-parameter emulator for the nonlinear matter power spectrum with a physically motivated electron prescription to construct a cosmology-dependent cosmic-DM distribution. Within this unified analysis framework, the mean and variance of DM respond self-consistently to the same underlying cosmology, directly connecting the FRB likelihood to both cosmic expansion and structure growth. Analyzing 125 localized FRBs at $0.105\leq z\leq2.148$, we obtain $\Omega_m = 0.33^{+0.10}_{-0.11}$ and $w = -0.80^{+0.28}_{-0.38}$ under the flat $w$CDM model. We find a new positive $\Omega_m-w$ degeneracy in the FRB posterior, opposite to the strong anticorrelation derived from Type Ia supernovae, offering a complementary test of dark energy properties and highlighting their potential in future precision cosmological studies.
papers.authors: Yi-Ying Wang, Shi-Jie Gao, Chi Zhang, Yi-Zhong Fan

papers.title: Design and Forecasts for a Rubin Twilight Program for Nearby Type Ia Supernovae
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.25317v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nearby Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) are important for supernova cosmology, but saturation in 30 s exposures, gaps in light-curve sampling, and the footprint of Vera C. Rubin Observatory's baseline Wide-Fast-Deep (WFD) survey limit the nearby sample. To improve the low-$z$ sample, we propose a twilight follow-up program using Rubin Observatory for 1-5 s griz exposures at solar altitudes $-12^\circ \le \mathrm{Alt}_\odot \le -9^\circ$. Using simulations of one year of WFD observations, we find that twilight follow-up adds 230 quality-selected SNe Ia from an external sample drawn primarily from the Transient Name Server (TNS). At $z<0.08$, the usable sample increases from 368 to 643 SNe Ia, including 50 WFD events recovered by refitting their light curves with twilight photometry. Combining these twilight observations with high-redshift WFD and Deep Drilling Field samples increases the statistical-only dark-energy $(w_0,w_a)$ figure of merit from 49.3 to 58.3 (18%) and reduces $\sigma(w_a)$ by 10%. For measurements of structure growth at $0.02 \le z<0.06$, the fractional uncertainty on $f\sigma_8$ decreases from 0.783 to 0.305. Restricting the program to $-12^\circ \le \mathrm{Alt}_\odot \le -11^\circ$ reduces the dark-energy improvement to 7.2%. These short exposures could also provide unsaturated photometry of potential distance-ladder calibrators at $z<0.02$.
papers.authors: Xianzhe TZ Tang, Dillon Brout, Christopher W. Stubbs, Elana K. Urbach, J. Bryce Kalmbach, Greg Aldering, Bastien Carreres, Chris Frohmaier, Ayan Mitra, Erik R. Peterson, Corentin Ravoux, the LSST Dark Energy Science Collaboration

papers.title: The Universality of Halo Growth and Merger Rates in Modified Gravity Theories
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.25472v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the standard $\Lambda$CDM framework, the merger rate of dark matter haloes has been found to follow a nearly universal form, with only weak dependence on halo mass and redshift. We examine whether this universality is preserved in modified gravity (MG) models, where the growth of cosmic structure can deviate from that of general relativity (GR). We use the ELEPHANT suite of large $N$-body simulations to study halo merger rates and mass accretion histories in different modified gravity models, including two representative scenarios beyond-GR: the Hu--Sawicki chameleon $f(R)$ model and the normal branch of the Dvali--Gabadadze--Porrati model. For the mass accretion histories, the modified gravitational effect can produce systematic departures from GR, generally corresponding to more rapid halo growth. The deviations are relatively small when the MG effect is weak, while they become more pronounced in models with strong deviation from GR and can exceed $15\%$ in the extreme case. For the halo merger rate, we find that the nearly universal behavior is well preserved across all the gravity models, with only weak dependence on redshift and halo mass, reflecting the unbiased accretion nature of halo growth. However, apparent deviation from this universality can arise if the halo mass is not defined consistently with the modified gravity model.
papers.authors: Haicong Xu, Yechun Yong, Feihong He, Zhongxu Zhai, Jiaxin Han, Baojiu Li

papers.title: Upper Bounds on the Radion Mass in a Warped Extra Dimension
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2611.25473v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study absolute upper bounds on the mass ratio $R_{11}=m_{r_1}/m_{h_1}$ between the radion ($r_1$) and graviton ($h_1$) lightest modes in five dimensional warped models. We consider warped models with an admissible singular behavior in the infrared: i.e.~models with power-like ($\sim  ar\phi^{2n}$) and with exponential ($\sim e^{2
u ar\phi}$) bulk potentials, where $ ar\phi$ is the stabilizing bulk field. We find a correlation between $R_{11}$ and the singular behavior of the Ricci scalar, which allows to establish an absolute upper bound on the former. For the power-like models, the maximum value of $R_{11}$ increases with $n$. In the limit $n	o\infty$, the power-like model reproduces the exponential model and reaches the same upper bound as the latter. For the exponential model, we derive analytically the bound $R_{11}<1$, with the largest value approached for the case $
u	o 1^+$ (where $
u=1$ corresponds to the linear dilaton model) and consistent with unitarity sum rules. For exponential models we also obtain the absolute upper bound on the second radion mode ratio $R_{21}=m_{r_2}/m_{h_1}\lesssim 1.374$. This value is reached for $
u=2$ when the IR brane approaches the singularity. For this configuration, we verify that the scalar contribution satisfies the unitarity sum rule when the complete radion Kaluza-Klein tower is included.
papers.authors: Leandro Da Rold, Eugenio Megias, Mariano Quiros, Lindber Salas

papers.title: Pairwise fermionic mode correlations in electric and magnetic backgrounds: Landau-level structure and Schwinger production
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.25507v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate mutual information and logarithmic negativity in fermionic Schwinger pair production in parallel electric and magnetic fields. Using spin-dependent Bogoliubov transformations, we construct the in-vacuum and derive the particle--antiparticle correlations for selected Landau modes. We also consider an initially entangled two-particle state and evaluate the correlations for six bipartitions. The physical Landau-level structure is treated explicitly by distinguishing modes with the same oscillator index from the spin representatives of a common physical Landau level. For matched higher levels, the pairwise redistribution relations retain the electric-only form, with the magnetic-field dependence entering through the Landau-level pair-production probabilities. When the two particle groups occupy different physical levels, the cross particle--antiparticle correlations become unequal, and we derive analytic relations characterizing this asymmetry. We further obtain the local logarithmic negativity from the ordinary partial transpose in a fixed occupation-space basis. Finally, we extend the analysis to a Sauter-type electric field in a constant magnetic background and examine the dependence of the pairwise correlations on the field parameters and Landau-level structure.
papers.authors: Sahil Chetan Patnekar, Sristi Sanjivanee Goswami, Sanjay Pant, Shagun Kaushal

papers.title: Thermodynamic topology and orbital dynamics of charged RN--AdS black hole with logarithmic corrections
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.25518v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study investigates the topological thermodynamic properties and orbital dynamics of the Reissner--Nordstr\"{o}m anti-de Sitter (RN--AdS) black hole with logarithmic corrections solution in Einstein--Maxwell gravity. By utilizing the Duan's $\Phi$-mapping theory, we investigate the topological classes within the generalized three-parameter Sharma--Mittal entropy formalism. Employing different thermodynamic ensembles, including the canonical and mixed canonical ensembles, we explore the critical, divergence points and heat capacity, which help us determine the thermodynamic stability of the BH. In addition, the Hamiltonian formalism is employed to investigate the orbital and oscillatory motion of neutral test particles. By utilizing the effective potential approach, we examine the effective force, the stability of circular orbits, and the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO). We further analyze the trajectories of test particles and derive the radial $\left(\omega_{r}\right)$, latitudinal $\left(\omega_{\theta}\right)$, and azimuthal $\left(\omega_{\phi}\right)$ oscillation frequencies, together with the periastron precession frequency. This work provides key insights into the fundamental nature of Einstein--Maxwell gravity. Moreover, these results provide a comprehensive theoretical description of the orbital dynamics of the RN--AdS black hole solution and may be useful for future high-precision astrophysical observations.
papers.authors: Hafiza Bushra Mujahid, Muhammad Yasir, Shahid Qaisar, Faisal Javed

papers.title: From Integrability to Chaos in Tensionless AdS3 String Theory
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.25576v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study quantum-gravitational corrections to the planar integrable structure of the symmetric product orbifold $\text{Sym}^N(\mathbb{T}^4)$ that is dual to tensionless string theory on AdS$_3\times$S$^3\times \mathbb{T}^4$. We consider the deformation that switches on R-R flux in the bulk, and analyze the associated level spacing statistics. The leading non-planar corrections lift the planar degeneracies and produce signs of random-matrix behavior. Our results provide a controlled example of string interactions driving the onset of quantum chaos.
papers.authors: Matthias R. Gaberdiel, Beat Nairz, Cheng Peng

papers.title: A full-color four-point form factor
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.25591v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the symbol and complete functions of the full-color two-loop four-point maximally helicity violating stress-tensor form factor in $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang-Mills theory, including $N^1$ double traces and $N^0$ single traces. Numerical unitarity and a master-integral bootstrap fix the result. A direct form-factor bootstrap reproduces the symbol. Permuting external legs in the planar 88-letter alphabet yields all 79 letters, while the $N^0$ terms contain four new nonclassical contributions. We also obtain the complete $N^0$ two-loop triple-collinear hard splitting functions.
papers.authors: Song He, Xuhang Jiang

papers.title: Two Faces of Spacetime Density Matrices: Entanglement and Complexity
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.25634v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a direct connection between entanglement and complexity through spacetime density matrices. For stationary pure states and complementary regions at different times, spacetime replica moments encode the return amplitude of a replica-defect quench. This representation defines an associated state spread complexity, which we call Krylov-R\'enyi complexity. It can equivalently be obtained by using a replica-defect excitation of the replicated background state as the seed and evolving it under the original replicated Hamiltonian. We further construct Krylov-von Neumann complexity as a probe limit from first-order replica data. Timelike entanglement and complexity provide complementary information at a fixed time, while the full time dependence of the timelike entropy determines the Krylov dynamics and hence the complexity. The replica construction fixes the seed and its evolution through the background state, subsystem geometry, and regulator, without an independently chosen probe operator. Like entanglement entropy, the resulting complexity is defined nonperturbatively and probes universal properties and dynamical information about the underlying theory.
papers.authors: Wu-zhong Guo

papers.title: Second-order formulation of chiral fermions with a local boundary condition
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.25749v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chiral fermions in $d$ dimensions arise naturally as boundary modes of a massive fermion in $d+1$ dimensions subject to a local boundary condition. When anomalies are absent, this construction can be used to define an intrinsically $d$-dimensional theory of chiral fermions. However, defining the path integral using the first-order Dirac operator with this boundary condition is technically inconvenient, even in the continuum. We present a formulation in terms of second-order differential operators that is completely equivalent to the original formulation in the continuum. Its natural lattice discretization generates Wilson's term and avoids fermion doubling. Our lattice formulation closely resembles the boundary-fermion construction of Shamir, and provides some insight into the case of a general Wilson parameter.
papers.authors: Kazuya Yonekura

papers.title: Phase transitions in self-gravitating objects and black holes: Common properties and interpretations
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.25786v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a simple analytic two-component model that links the thermal evolution of self-gravitating systems to black-hole thermodynamics. The model consists of a monatomic nonrelativistic ideal gas and an effective barotropic support calibrated by the specific heat $\hat c_V^{\rm J}(\Theta)$ of a J\"uttner gas. From the partition function we obtain an exact modified Bessel expression for $\hat c_V^{\rm J}(\Theta)$ and supply compact Pad\'e approximants with good accuracy across all temperatures. These inputs yield a closed virial-capacity formula, which we use to determine where the heat capacity changes sign as the support pressure becomes competitive with the thermal pressure. We then contrast this behavior with Schwarzschild anti-de Sitter black holes. Despite the disparate microphysics, both systems exhibit a switch in heat-capacity behavior governed by competing pressure contributions. The surrogate model provides compact analytic insight into stability thresholds in self-gravitating systems and their black-hole analogues.
papers.authors: Martin Blaschke, Petr Slan\'y

papers.title: Square Kilometre Array Science Data Challenge 3b: EoR inference
papers.abstract: arXiv:2611.25823v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present and analyse the results of Science Data Challenge 3b (SDC3b; https://sdc3.skao.int/challenges/inference), an Epoch of Reionization (EoR) inference exercise organised by the Square Kilometre Array Observatory (SKAO) using simulated SKA data. The nine-month challenge, running from October 2024 to May 2025, represents the first community-wide comparison of EoR inference pipelines on common simulated datasets. We consider multiple datasets designed to assess performance on both foreground-free and foreground-contaminated cylindrical power spectra and imaging products, adopting different reionization scenarios and EoR simulation models. We include results from 16 teams, which employ a range of methodologies to infer the posterior distribution of the hydrogen neutral fraction across three redshift intervals spanning z=8.41 to z=6.25. The results show significant inter-team variability of the astrophysical constraints even in the simpler case where only instrumental noise is added to the cosmological signal. This underscores the need for further investigation into the relative contributions of signal modelling, the treatment of instrumental effects, and inference methods to the robustness of the resulting conclusions. Although individual methods can produce biased parameter estimates, the combined average of their estimates remains close to the input values, suggesting that independent approaches can offset method-specific biases.
